text:
henry: noticing strange GPU fragmentation in ap-south1a over the last hour — lots of tiny pods pending and sudden eviction bursts. chart shows one rack with very few free slots while others idle.
sophia: any recent taint/affinity changes for that rack?
henry: we pushed a taint `rack-exclusive=true:NoSchedule` to enforce rack-locality for a particular reserved pool earlier today. intended to reduce noisy-neighbor cross-traffic.
raj: that could explain it if some tiny pods require GPU and scheduler is over-constraining. Are pods marked with `preferredDuringScheduling` affinities? if so those can be ignored and still schedule somewhere else.
henry: many tiny pods use a hard nodeSelector gpu:true and tolerate the taint via `Effect=NoSchedule` with a matching toleration, but we forgot to add the equivalent label to the other racks — so only one rack qualifies.
telemetry-bot: ALERT: binpack.fragmentation.ap-south1a p99 increased 4.5x, evictions.ap-south1a spike 310 over 30m. https://monitoring/redwood/frag-ap-south1a :warning:
sophia: ok immediate mitigation options: (1) remove rack-exclusive taint (fast but may reintroduce traffic interference), (2) add label to other racks and phase in taint, (3) add a soft-affinity fallback so pods can use any GPU if wait > 60s.
raj: I like (3) as short term. We can patch scheduler's schedulingPolicy for tiny pods: allow fallback after `maxWait=60s` and set `fallbackNodePool=global-gpu`. That avoids mass evictions.
henry: applying (3) now: patch scheduler config -> `scheduler.policies.tinyPod.maxWait=60s` and `scheduler.policies.tinyPod.fallbackPool=global-gpu`.
infra: patch applied by henry at 6901234635, rolling.
telemetry-bot: NOTE: change deployed at 6901234642. watch metrics for 15m.
sophia: also going to add the missing label to racks `rack-group=low-noise` so we can re-enable taint more safely across racks. rolling label update to racks 3/5 now.
henry: metrics so far: evictions down from 310 -> 72 in 10m, pending tiny pods reduced 65%. fragmentation p95 down 9%.
raj: follow-ups: infra add pre-deploy check to ensure taint target label coverage >= 90%, scheduler add grace-based fallback for constrained pools, and run a canary that simulates rack-label mismatch in staging. I'll file those.
oncall: creating incident for tracking and assigning follow-ups: infra(adding labels) -> sophia, scheduler(policy fallback) -> raj, cost(impact of fallback) -> henry. keep thread updated. :lock:
